_README: Deliberate answers to table-name collisions found by tools/schema-collisions.js.
A collision happens when two migrations declare the same table. PostgreSQL's
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS silently skips the second one, so its columns are
never created and the migration still reports success. Somebody has to decide
what the collision MEANT. This file records those decisions so the checker
does not re-report a question that has already been answered, and so the next
person can see the reasoning instead of guessing.
synonym  - the losing column is the same fact under a different name.
DO NOT add it. Two columns holding one number will drift.
merged   - the losing columns were genuinely new and have been added to the
winning table by an explicit ALTER. Record where.
renamed  - the two tables were different concepts that happened to share a
name. The later one was renamed. Record the new name.
deferred - genuinely different concepts sharing a name, or a same-concept
table with real risk (mismatched FK types, heavy cross-references)
not yet safe to merge or rename without a live database to verify
against. Recorded so CI is not blocked on an open question, but this
is NOT a completed decision - real reconciliation work remains.

decisions.rationale: 047 uses buyer/seller vocabulary, 028 uses customer/supplier. Same facts. 028 wins because it runs first and is the more normalised of the two (028 stores the tax split in columns; 047 stores it in a gst_calculation JSONB blob). eway_bill_number was genuinely absent from 028 and has been added — an e-way bill is legally required above Rs 50,000 and is asked for at inter-state check posts.

Identical tax fields, shorter names. taxable_value was genuinely absent: 028 records total_amount and discount_amount but not the assessable base between them, which GSTR returns and e-invoice IRN payloads both require. Deriving it at read time invites two callers deriving it differently.

Merged rather than renamed, because these are one entity seen from two sides: 015 holds the agreement (parties, terms, value, currency) and 019 holds where that agreement lives on chain (address, abi, network, tx hash). 015 already carried blockchain_hash, so the two were always describing the same artifact. Contrast ai_predictions below, which was renamed because the two were unrelated.
decisions.note: These columns appear absent when the migration chain is applied without the pgcrypto extension, because 019 aborts at its CREATE EXTENSION line and its ALTERs never run. That is an environment gap, not a schema gap. CI provisions pgcrypto.

decisions.rationale: 000's ai_predictions logs ML model inferences (model_type, features_used, model_version). 990 needed a calibration ledger for agent forecasts (stated_confidence, ape_pct, input_quality) — a different thing that happened to want the same name. Merging them would have produced one table where most columns are null for most rows, which is how the other collisions in this list were created. Renamed instead. The view v_ai_calibration failed with 'column actor_id does not exist' until this was fixed; the error pointed at the view, not at the collision that caused it, which is exactly why the checker exists.

Three files declare demand_forecasts for three different things: 015 stores ML model output (forecast_data JSONB, accuracy, model_version), 030 stores institutional menu planning, and 052 stores a scalar regional quantity for a date. 015 wins because it runs first and other code already reads it. 052's four columns are additive scalars rather than competing spellings, so they are added by ALTER rather than dropped. Note that 015's 'accuracy' and 052's 'confidence' are NOT the same measure — accuracy is observed after the fact, confidence is claimed before it — and averaging them would produce a number that means nothing.
decisions.note: Caught by tools/schema-collisions.js after 999_economic_layer.sql was added. The file was also renumbered from 999 to 052: it shared the 999_ prefix with 999_schema_reconciliation.sql, and reconciliation must run last.

decisions.rationale: 3102's promotions is a marketing/discount-code table; 3200's is an employee career-promotion history table (previous_role/new_role/promotion_date/approved_by) - unrelated concepts sharing a name. Renamed the HR table to employee_promotions and updated its one real caller, hrService.js's getEmployee() JOIN, and the file's own indexes.

3200's departments is the live HR department table (department_name/department_code/manager_id, queried for real by hrService.js). 996's is an unused multi-tenant scaffold (company_id/business_unit_id/head_user_id UUID, parent_department_id self-FK) with zero real callers - confirmed via grep, the only other hit was a string literal in M004's array, not a SQL reference. Renamed 996's version and its 3 internal FK references to enterprise_departments to avoid inventing a UUID head_user_id column on a table hrService.js's INTEGER-keyed employees actually use.

Same RBAC roles concept; 015's extra columns are genuinely additive. This file already had a repair migration recovering is_system_role/level/metadata/updated_at from a prior session - it just hadn't caught hierarchy_level/default_permissions yet, which is why 015's own seed INSERT (line 156) would have failed with 'column does not exist' against a real database. Extended the existing repair file rather than creating a new one.

1001's key/value are the same facts as 014's config_key/config_value under different names - NOT duplicated per this file's synonym rule. description/environment are genuinely new, added via ALTER. 1001's own seed INSERT referenced key/value/description/environment, none of which existed on the winning table, so it would fail 'column does not exist' against a real database; rewritten to target config_key/config_value/config_type instead.

Both losers' users tables are largely subsets/near-duplicates of the winner (same UUID id, same core fields) with only a couple of genuinely new columns (e.g. 1000's `name`). Low risk to merge, but not verified against a live database this session - deferred rather than guessed at 4am.

Different concept AND a real pre-existing bug: 3019's version declares `user_id INTEGER REFERENCES users(id)` but users.id is UUID - that CREATE TABLE would fail a type check on any database where it actually ran, independent of the collision. Needs a real column-type fix, not a blind merge or rename.

Same RBAC-assignment concept; loser adds id/expires_at/is_active as plain extra columns (not a PK change - winner keeps its own composite PK). Likely safe to merge but not verified against a live database this session.

Different concept: winner is the platform's core farmer entity (UUID, FDI scoring, linked to users/fpos, referenced by iot_devices/training_records/dpr_documents/contract_milestones and many other tables). Loser is a standalone SERIAL-keyed registration-form table with no FK to users. Given how many other tables FK into farmers(id), a merge or rename here needs careful review with a live database, not a same-night guess.

Different concept: winner tracks farmer agricultural training (UUID, farmer_id FK); loser tracks employee HR training (SERIAL, employee_id/training_program_id FK), used for real by hrService.js. A real table, needs an intentional rename (e.g. employee_training_records) with its own migration + service-reference update, not done this pass.

Different concept and different PK type (UUID vs VARCHAR(50)): winner is a general contract/escrow milestone table; loser is ecommerce-specific (contract_farming FK, quality_verified, payment_status), used for real by ecommerceBusinessSalesService.js. Needs an intentional rename with its own migration + service-reference update, not done this pass.

Same audit-logging concept across all three; the two losers each add 1-2 plain extra columns (error_message; entity/details). Likely safe to merge but not verified against a live database this session, and audit_logs is compliance-sensitive enough to want that verification first.

Different PK type (SERIAL vs VARCHAR(50)) and part of a broader, already-documented review-system duplication (.ai/tasks/ACTIVE.md already flags M060 Review Management vs services/legacy/productReviewService.js as an unreconciled duplicate). Deferred to the same follow-up rather than adding a third variant of the reconciliation tonight.
Same 3100_ecommerce_tables.sql VARCHAR(50)-PK family as product_reviews above - deferred alongside it for the same reason.
Same 3100_ecommerce_tables.sql VARCHAR(50)-PK family as product_reviews above - deferred alongside it for the same reason.

Likely the same concept (only bin_location is genuinely lost per the checker), but the two versions use different product/warehouse FK types (products UUID vs product_listings VARCHAR(50)) suggesting they serve two different catalog subsystems that happen to share a table name. Deferred rather than assumed-safe without a live database to verify the ALTER against.

Likely the same GDPR-consent concept with genuinely additive columns, but 3017's version declares user_id as INTEGER against a UUID users.id - the same latent type bug found in user_profiles. Needs the same real-column-type review before merging.

Likely the same concept, but 3030's lost farmer_id column is declared INTEGER REFERENCES farmers(id) against a UUID farmers.id - same latent type bug pattern. A merge needs to add farmer_id as UUID, not copy the loser's literal (broken) type - not done this pass without a live database to confirm.

Different concept despite matching UUID PK: winner is a bank/investor engineering-project DPR (project_id, total_project_cost, target_institution); loser is a farmer-financing DPR (farmer_id, crop_plan_id, financing_ask_inr), used for real by dprGenerationService.js and foluBenchmarkService.js. Needs an intentional rename with its own migration + multi-file service-reference update, not done this pass.
Same 3100_ecommerce_tables.sql VARCHAR(50)-PK family noted under product_reviews above - deferred for the same reason (different catalog subsystem, needs dedicated review).
Different PK type (BIGSERIAL vs UUID) suggesting two independently-built climate subsystems sharing a name. Deferred pending a review of which is actually live.

Likely the same MFA-secret concept with genuinely additive columns (phone_number/enabled/enabled_at/disabled_at) and matching column types this time - lower risk than most of this list, but not verified against a live database this session.

Different concept despite matching SERIAL PK: winner is a flat debit/credit ledger line (one row per DEBIT or CREDIT); loser is a formal multi-tenant journal-entry header (company_id, fiscal_period_id, journal_type, presumably paired with a separate lines table not in this collision). Part of the same 995/996 'recovered ERP' vs 3102 'ecommerce ERP' duplication as purchase_orders/production_orders below - needs a coordinated rename across all three, not done this pass.

Different concept and different PK type (VARCHAR(50) vs SERIAL): winner is a simple B2B marketplace purchase request (seller_id, requested_quantity); loser is a formal procurement PO with requisition/RFQ chain (po_number, vendor_id, approved_by), used for real by ecommerceERPService.js under the SAME bare 'purchase_orders' name the winner also uses - meaning ecommerceERPService.js's own queries are ambiguous about which schema they expect. Needs careful review of ecommerceERPService.js against both table shapes before any rename, not done this pass.
Same 995/996 vs 3102 ERP duplication as purchase_orders and journal_entries above - deferred alongside them pending a coordinated review.
Different PK type (UUID vs SERIAL) suggesting two independently-built cold-storage booking systems. Deferred pending a review of which is actually live.

decisions.loser: 031_iot_integration_schema.sql (ALTERs merged), 3030_m030_farmer_advisory.sql (no-op, farmer_id INTEGER type already flagged bad)
decisions.rationale: 072_tier1_m025_m030_schema.sql added farmer_id/specifications/registered_at/last_active as real ALTER columns so iotIntegrationService.js's hardcoded raw-SQL column names resolve. That is NOT the same as resolving the underlying model conflict: iotIntegrationService.js links a device to its owner via farmer_id, while digitalTwinService.js's getIoTDataForEntity() queries `iot_devices WHERE entity_id = $1` - a column that still does not exist anywhere and was deliberately not added, because adding a bare entity_id with no entity_type companion would be ambiguous (a farm and a crop could collide on the same UUID). Two same-day Devin services disagree on this table's ownership model; someone has to decide whether digital-twin IoT lookups should go through farmer_id (via the twin's owner_id) or a real polymorphic entity_id/entity_type pair before digitalTwinService.getIoTDataForEntity() can work.
decisions.note: See .claude/audits/AUDIT_DB.md finding #3 and .ai/tasks/ACTIVE.md for the full analysis.
decisions.resolution_2026_08_31: Decided: farmer_id, not a new entity_id/entity_type pair. Every digital_twins row already has owner_id (the twin's farmer, UUID FK to farmers) regardless of whether the twin is a farm or a crop - so getRealWorldData() now passes twin.owner_id into getIoTDataForEntity(), and that method queries iot_devices WHERE farmer_id = $1 instead of the nonexistent entity_id. No migration needed - this uses a column that already exists and is already populated by iotIntegrationService.registerDevice(). Rejected the entity_id/entity_type alternative because nothing would ever populate it (device registration is farmer-scoped, not twin-scoped) - it would have been a second unused column, the same fabrication-adjacent smell already flagged elsewhere in this codebase. Implemented in backend/src/services/digitalTwinService.js.

decisions.rationale: sensor_data (031) and iot_sensor_data (072, matching iotIntegrationService.js's actual writes) are the same real-world concept - sensor readings - but not safe to merge: sensor_data.device_id is an INTEGER FK to iot_devices.id (the surrogate key), while iotIntegrationService.js writes/reads the business device_id STRING directly with no surrogate-key lookup step. They also disagree semantically on 'quality' (031: a 0-100 anomaly score; iotIntegrationService.js: a good/out_of_range/invalid enum). Created as two separate tables rather than guessing which linking strategy wins. Reconcile once IoT ingestion is actually live and one device-linking strategy is chosen platform-wide.

decisions.loser: N/A - no competing migration exists; advancedAnalyticsService.js and predictiveIntelligenceService.js were written against a table that was never built
decisions.rationale: advancedAnalyticsService.js and predictiveIntelligenceService.js query crops.farmer_id, crops.expected_yield_kg, crops.planting_date, crops.growth_stage, orders.farmer_id, orders.region, order_items.crop_id, order_items.price_per_kg, and a `harvests` table - none of which exist. The real crops table (041) is a static catalog (crop_code, common_name, category, duration_days), not a per-farmer planted-crop instance with yield/harvest tracking; orders.user_id and order_items.product_id are the real columns, with no crop_id. This is not a missing-migration gap, it's a schema design gap: a crop_plantings/crop_cycles table (farmer_id, crop_id FK to the catalog, planting_date, expected_yield_kg, growth_stage, harvest records) needs to be designed before either service can run. Not attempted in 072_tier1_m025_m030_schema.sql - bolting 10+ unrelated columns onto the catalog table was explicitly avoided per this file's own no-guessing convention.
decisions.note: Also blocks digitalTwinService.js's farm-twin path, which separately depends on a `farms` table that does not exist at all (no CREATE TABLE anywhere) and joins crops ON f.id = c.farm_id, a column crops does not have either. See .claude/audits/AUDIT_DB.md findings #1 and #6, and .ai/tasks/ACTIVE.md.
decisions.resolution_2026_08_31_partial: Built farms + crop_plantings (9999_zzzz..._farms_crop_plantings_schema.sql) and rewired digitalTwinService.js's verifyFarm/getFarmRealTimeData/verifyCrop/getCropRealTimeData against them - that consumer is now fully closed (crop twins reference a crop_plantings.id, not the catalog crops.id). Deliberately did NOT touch advancedAnalyticsService.js or predictiveIntelligenceService.js in the same pass: their crop queries invent a THIRD, different imagined shape directly on `crops` (crop_type/variety/quality_grade/growing_period_days/climate_requirements - none of which crop_plantings has either, since it stores a growth instance, not catalog metadata), plus a `harvests` table that doesn't exist, plus order_items.crop_id where the real column is order_items.product_id. Fixing those needs a separate decision (how orders/order_items relate to crops vs products) that would be guessed, not verified, if made in the same pass as this one - left deferred on purpose.

decisions.rationale: Same real-world concept (a marketplace buyer entity) declared twice; 041 runs first alphabetically/numerically so strategic_services_schema.sql's richer CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS buyers (organization_type, credit_rating, annual_procurement_volume, status) silently no-ops against a live database. Verified NOT currently a runtime bug: the 4 strategic services (preSeasonPurchaseService.js, contractFarmingService.js) only ever SELECT b.name from the buyers JOIN, and 041's buyers already has a name column. Deferred rather than merged because the extra columns (credit_rating etc.) are unused by any current query - adding them now would be speculative, not verified against an actual need.
decisions.note: Found while integrating the 31 Aug 2026 'Strategic Services' batch (pre-season purchase, contract farming, household procurement, government subsidy). If a future service starts reading strategic_services_schema.sql's buyers-specific columns, add them to 041's table via an ALTER repair migration (same pattern as the roles collision above), not by trying to make the second CREATE TABLE win.

decisions.rationale: Same collision shape as buyers above (033 runs first, its NABL-accreditation-focused laboratories table wins; strategic_services_schema.sql's simpler version no-ops). Verified NOT currently a runtime bug: the only reference is contract_quality_tests.laboratory_id UUID REFERENCES laboratories(id), and contractFarmingService.js only ever writes it as an optional value (testResult.laboratory_id || null) - it never queries laboratories' own columns, so which of the two column sets 'won' does not matter yet.
decisions.note: Found in the same pass as the buyers collision above. Revisit if a future feature needs to read laboratory-specific fields (accreditation_number/quality_rating from the losing definition vs nabl_accredited/testing_capabilities from the winning one).

decisions.table: digital_twins (duplicate service, not a table collision)
decisions.rationale: Not a migration collision (digital_twins is declared exactly once, in 072_tier1_m025_m030_schema.sql, entity_type/entity_id/owner_id/current_state) - a genuine duplicate SERVICE. services/legacy/digitalTwinService.js was written earlier against a digital_twins shape (farm_id, configuration, is_active) plus a `farms` table that has never existed in any migration - every DB-touching method in it has been broken since it was written, not since 072 landed. It was still live: required directly in index.js, initialize()'d at boot, and self-mounting routes via setupRoutes(app) at the exact prefix /api/v1/digital-twin the real service also uses. Most of its routes were silently shadowed (Express matches the real router, mounted first, before this one); the ones that didn't collide (bare POST/GET /api/v1/digital-twin, PUT /:twinId, POST /:twinId/sensor-data, GET /:twinId/simulations) were reachable and would 500 on every call.
decisions.resolution_2026_08_31: Un-mounted, not deleted. Removed the require/initialize()/setupRoutes() calls from index.js (kept the source file on disk, in case its simulation models - cropGrowthSimulation, soilMoistureSimulation, pestSpreadSimulation etc. - are worth porting into the real service later; the real one currently only has a subset). Verified: fresh backend boot clean, no ReferenceError from the removed variable, all other route mounting unaffected.
decisions.note: The real service's own farm/crop paths (createFarmDigitalTwin -> verifyFarm(), getFarmRealTimeData(); createCropDigitalTwin -> verifyCrop(), getCropRealTimeData()) are still blocked - they query a `farms` table and per-farmer crop-instance columns (crop_type, growth_stage, estimated_yield_kg, planting_date) that don't exist, for the exact same underlying reason as the 'crops (per-farmer planting model)' entry above. Same root cause as that entry, not a new one - see there for the real fix needed (a farms + crop_plantings schema).
